findings.claim: Classification preserved the original observation record and generated a later observation rather than rewriting the original evidence.
evidence: All classification records bind to the original classification observation b687545c-cb9d-4ad7-a6b9-e604ba95a0ed and retain its captured conditions and subtrees.
The post-classification material is a separate observation 21a32504-56bf-4d0f-aa5d-aa56998a5b51.

findings.claim: Classification did not clear discovery limitations or outstanding audit work.
evidence: The observation still reports STRUCTURAL_LIST_SCAN_TRUNCATED, multiple UNSUPPORTED_CANVAS gaps, and EVENT_LISTENER_COVERAGE.
The exploration audit remains blocked with discoveryComplete=false.
Current counts still include 159 awaiting_decision, 15 pending, 28 blocked, and 204 notAttempted.
Control coverage remains incomplete: 203 actionable, only 1 covered, and 202 incomplete.

limits: The change from 35 to 33 unconfirmed items reflects two active container classifications; it is not successful interaction coverage.
No inference is made that probe_required was probed, that interaction was executed, or that unresolved was resolved.
This verification proposes no new action, control review, classification, or scope decision.
overall: The classification behavior matches the protocol. Two non-action wrapper candidates moved from unconfirmed to container while their supported child links remained unexecuted. The other three classifications produced no action or automatic probe. ActionCount remains one for the modal Close; the two retired audit cases are older boundary-exit candidates and are unrelated to container classification. No issue was found in the reviewed materials.
